summary.text: Terrence Davis is the Democratic nominee for South Dakota secretary of state. A former state trooper in Tennessee and South Dakota who is pursuing a doctorate in law and policy, he was endorsed by Republican Secretary of State Monae Johnson.
He says he trusts the state's tested, audited vote-counting machines and wants to strengthen ties with county auditors, add a fraud-investigation division and let 16-year-olds pre-register.

paragraphs.text: Davis was born in Peoria, Illinois, and his campaign says he experienced homelessness as a child and that a foster mother helped him find a path forward.
He went to college as a non-traditional student and earned a degree in criminal justice, then a master's degree in public policy, and is now working on a doctorate in law and policy.
Davis served as a state trooper in Tennessee, working the Memphis District and the Executive Protection Unit that guards the governor and visiting officials.
His family moved to South Dakota in 2021, and he served as a trooper in the Sioux Falls district.
Most recently he worked at East River Legal Services, which helps South Dakotans get free civil legal help.
He lives in Sioux Falls with his wife, a public school teacher, and their son.

Johnson, a Republican who has worked in the Secretary of State's office for more than a decade, endorsed Davis on September 19, 2026, saying that although he is a Democrat, South Dakota deserves a secretary of state who will "strengthen confidence through performance rather than provocation."

Davis's priorities include keeping the state's audited ballot counters with post-election audits in every county, letting 16-year-olds pre-register when they get a driver's license, creating an investigative division for fraud, and updating the office's systems for businesses and nonprofits.
